Definition: from G4120; a plait (of hair):--broidered hair.
BiblicalUsage: Plegma is braided hair, a plait. Paul uses it once, in 1 Timothy 2:9, telling women to adorn themselves in modest apparel, not with broidered hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that modesty is an adornment no gold can buy.
